back: A program that optimizes another program is called an optimizer. Optimizers typically work at a low-level, looking for ways to improve statements or expressions by rewriting, reordering, or eliminating them.

Because hand-optimization is slow, programmers typically focuses on making high-level improvements that will have a large impact (such as choosing more performant algorithms, optimizing data storage and access, reducing resource utilization, parallelizing tasks, etc…)Other kinds of optimization can be performed automatically.
source_suffix: For example, when you write i = i * 2;, the optimizer might rewrite this as i *= 2;, i += i;, or i <<= 1;. For integral values, all of these produce the same result, but one might be faster than the others on a given architecture. A programmer would probably not know which is the most performant choice (and the answer might vary based on architecture), but an optimizer for a given system would.
